name: Carnivorous plants — pitchers, sundews, snap traps
status: 13 archetypal species (full list archived in docs/plant_archive)
notes: Bog and seep plants that live where the soil has no nitrogen and take it from insects instead. Rule they add: they grow ONLY on nutrient-poor ground (peat, sand, wet rock, tepui summits) with high moisture, and their growth reads the local INSECT count instead of soil fertility — a bog full of midges grows fat pitchers; kill the insects and the sundews starve. Their flowers stand far above the traps so the pollinators survive. Sarracenia and Dionaea live in fire-kept pine savanna and bog and need the burns (Phase 9 reads this). Nepenthes are tropical climbers and cliff plants; the great montane ones drown rats and host tree shrews. Bladderworts float in ponds and eat water fleas.
